answer.summary: Claire distinguishes routine, functional information-sharing—which AI can synthesize and distribute—from human communication that persuades, inspires, and gets people aligned to act.

sections.heading: Communication AI may take over
sections.content: Her “lowercase C” is the functional exchange of information people need to do their jobs. She says AI is good at synthesizing information, assembling communications, coordinating their recipients, and delivering them in different formats. It can also help distill information into a plan and communicate that plan.

sections.heading: Communication that still depends on people
sections.content: Her “capital C” is the human work of being influential and convincing, showing boldness, and getting a group of people to follow a path. She also points to seeing a future beyond what a model trained on prior examples can envision, plus charisma and attracting others to make an idea happen. These are much harder to replicate, particularly when a PM needs to get buy-in and align people.

sections.heading: Illustration and implication for PMs
sections.content: Vo contrasts those human strengths with routine, well-understood work: she says she need not use her uniquely human skills to invent a standard way to export data to Snowflake; AI can scaffold it, after which the team can customize and ship it. She expects PM value to shift toward building the right things quickly and ensuring they deliver, whatever tools are used—not simply manifesting ideas personally.
